data.name: Adonai
data.gender_notes: Adonai is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Adonai is a title for God, meaning 'Lord' or 'Master'. It is used extensively throughout the Old Testament to refer to God as the supreme ruler and sovereign of the universe. The name Adonai carries the meaning “Lord, Master” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Adonai usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, master and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing God's sovereignty and control over our lives.
data.etymology: Adonai belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord, Master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adonai total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: אדוני
in_hebrew.meaning: אדוני ה' הוא שם פועל של אלוהים בעברית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אדוני ה' הוא אחד משמותיו של אלוהים בתנ'ך העברי, המשמש ככינוי למלכותו וריבונו של אלוהים. הוא מורכב משורש אדון שפירושו 'אדון' או 'ריבונו', ומשמש ככינוי לאלוהים כריבונו של עולם.

in_greek.name: Αδωναϊ
in_greek.meaning: Αδωναϊ σημαίνει Κύριος και Θεός στα Ελληνικά
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Αδωναϊ είναι μία μορφή του ονόματος του Θεού στην Ελληνική Βίβλο, προερχόμενη από την Εβραϊκή λέξη אדוני (Adonai). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο όρος χρησιμοποιείται ως μία μορφή σεβασμού και τιμής προς τον Θεό, αναδεικνύοντας τη σχέση του Θεού με την ανθρωπότητα.

in_latin.name: Adonai
in_latin.meaning: Adonai significat Dominus et Deus in Latino
in_latin.long_meaning: Adonai est unum de nomina Dei in traditione christiana, derivatum ex Hebraeo אדוני (Adonai). In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Adonai usitatum erat ad designandum Dominum Deum, cum reverentia et honore.

in_english.name: Adonai
in_english.meaning: Lord and Master, a title of God in the Christian tradition
in_english.long_meaning: Adonai is a Hebrew name for God, meaning 'Lord' or 'Master', signifying God's sovereignty and dominion. In Christian tradition, Adonai is used to emphasize God's lordship and authority. The name Adonai has been adopted in various Christian cultures, symbolizing reverence and worship.

data.cultural_impact: In Jewish tradition, the name Adonai is considered too sacred to be spoken aloud, and instead, the word Adonai is replaced with the word Adon or the Hebrew letter Hay or He (�� kör ה ), making it a custom during prayer and other religious practices to substitute this title when reading or speaking God's name.
data.spiritual_significance: Adonai represents the idea of God as a loving but powerful ruler, the one who is in control of all things and yet intimately involved in the lives of His people. It signifies the deep reverence and awe that people have for the true God – the creator and sustainer of the universe. Adonai is a reminder of God's sovereignty and the trust and submission that should be placed in Him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adonai is a Hebrew term meaning "Lord" or "Master." In Christianity, it is used as a title for God, emphasizing His sovereignty and authority over all creation. It serves as a reminder of our submission and dependence on Him.

biblical_reference.note: In the Hebrew Bible, Adonai is used as a substitute for the Tetragrammaton (YHWH) to emphasize God's transcendence and holiness.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, the name Adonai (Hebrew: אֲדֹנָי) is used as a title for God, meaning 'Lord' or 'Master'. It is derived from the Hebrew verb 'adon', which means 'to rule' or 'to possess'. The use of this title is common in the Hebrew Bible, and it is often translated as 'Lord' in English versions of the text.

The name Adonai also appears in the New Testament, specifically in the book of Acts. In Acts 5:2-3, Ananias and Sapphira lie to the apostles Peter and the Holy Spirit reveals their deceit. Peter responds, 'Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back part of the proceeds of the land? While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not under your control? Why have you conceived this scheme in your heart? You have not lied to man but to God.' Here, Adonai is used interchangeably with 'God'.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term Adonai is primarily used in modern contexts as a reverential name for God in Jewish and Christian traditions. It is often used in prayer, worship music, and scholarly study of religious texts. The term carries a sense of power, majesty, and sovereignty, and is seen as a way to connect with the divine. Adonai is also of interest to those studying ancient Hebrew language and religious history, as it is one of the many names of God used in the Hebrew Bible. In contemporary usage, Adonai is found in various platforms, including Jewish synagogues and prayer services, Christian churches and worship music, and academic and scholarly contexts.
